models.name: BookBrief
models.description: What to write — title, audience, and how many chapters.

fields.name: genre
fields.description: Genre / form e.g. cozy mystery novella

fields.name: chapter_count
fields.description: How many chapters to outline and write (keep small for demos)

models.name: ChapterOutline
models.description: One planned chapter from the initial chapter list.

models.name: ChapterJob
models.description: One batch item — chapter outline plus book-level context for the writer.

models.name: ChapterDraft
models.description: One written chapter as markdown body.

fields.name: title
fields.description: Chapter title used in the heading

fields.name: markdown
fields.description: Chapter BODY only (paragraphs / lists) — no # book title or ## chapter heading

models.name: BookManuscript
models.description: Full book joined into one markdown export.

fields.name: markdown
fields.description: Complete markdown manuscript ready to save as .md

modules.label: Brief
modules.inputDescription: JSON BookBrief — title, genre, audience, premise, tone, chapter_count
modules.note: Book parameters: title + how many chapters to write

modules.label: Outline Chapters
modules.note: BookBrief → list[ChapterOutline]. Initial chapter list for the whole book.
modules.inputDescription: BookBrief with title, premise, and chapter_count
modules.prompt:
Plan the full book as an ordered chapter list.
Return exactly chapter_count chapters (clamp to 1–12 if the brief is extreme).
Each chapter needs chapter_number (1-based), a vivid title, a short synopsis, and 2–5 concrete key_beats.
Keep arcs coherent across chapters: setup → rising action → climax → resolution for a short book.
Match genre, audience, premise, and tone from the brief.

modules.label: Enrich → Chapter Jobs
modules.note: list[ChapterOutline] → list[ChapterJob] — attach book-level context from Brief for each batch write.
modules.inputDescription: List of ChapterOutline objects from the outline step
modules.code: (chapters, state) => { const brief = state["Brief"] ?? {}; const title = String(brief?.title ?? "Untitled"); const genre = String(brief?.genre ?? ""); const audience = String(brief?.audience ?? ""); const premise = String(brief?.premise ?? ""); const tone = String(brief?.tone ?? ""); const rows = Array.isArray(chapters) ? chapters : []; const total = rows.length || Math.max(1, Number(brief?.chapter_count) || 1); return rows.map((c, i) => ({ chapter_number: Number(c?.chapter_number) || i + 1, title: String(c?.title ?? `Chapter ${i + 1}`), synopsis: String(c?.synopsis ?? ""), key_beats: Array.isArray(c?.key_beats) ? c.key_beats.map(String) : [], book_title: title, genre, audience, premise, tone, total_chapters: total })); }

modules.label: Write Each Chapter
modules.note: list[ChapterJob] → list[ChapterDraft]. One structured LLM call per chapter (parallel batch).
modules.inputDescription: List of ChapterJob objects — outline plus book context
modules.prompt:
Write ONE full chapter of the book described by book_title / genre / audience / premise / tone.
This is chapter chapter_number of total_chapters titled "title".
Follow the synopsis and hit every key_beat.
Keep chapter_number and title unchanged.
Return markdown as the chapter BODY only: prose paragraphs (and short lists if needed). Do NOT include a # book title or ## chapter heading — those are added when chapters are joined.
Aim for a short novella chapter (~400–900 words). Stay consistent with earlier/later chapter roles implied by chapter_number / total_chapters.

modules.label: Assemble Markdown Book
modules.note: list[ChapterDraft] → BookManuscript — single markdown export of the full book.
modules.inputDescription: List of ChapterDraft objects with markdown bodies

modules.label: Full Book Markdown
modules.inputDescription: Single BookManuscript — title, chapter_count, and complete markdown ready to export as .md
modules.note: Download markdown from the run output / shared link
